title: Indian Labour Law — Termination, Notice Period, and Employee Rights
source: Industrial Disputes Act 1947 & State Shops and Establishments Acts
content:
Employment in India is governed by a combination of Central laws (such as Industrial Disputes Act 1947, Industrial Employment Standing Orders Act 1946, Payment of Gratuity Act 1972) and State-specific laws (Shops and Establishments Acts of each state).

Termination and Retrenchment: Under the Industrial Disputes Act 1947, termination of a workman (non-managerial employee) by the employer for any reason other than disciplinary action is treated as retrenchment. Retrenchment requires: (1) One month's notice in writing or pay in lieu of notice, (2) Retrenchment compensation equal to 15 days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service, and (3) Notice to the appropriate government authority.

Notice Period & Wrongful Termination: For managerial/administrative employees not covered by the Industrial Disputes Act, notice periods and termination procedure are governed by the employment contract and the relevant State Shops and Establishments Act. Most State Acts mandate at least 30 days' notice or payment in lieu of notice after 3 to 6 months of continuous service. Sudden termination without notice or salary in lieu is illegal unless valid gross misconduct is proven after a fair internal inquiry.

Non-Payment of Salary & Full & Final (F&F) Settlement: Employers are legally obligated to clear all pending wages, accrued leave encashment, bonus, and statutory dues upon termination. State Shops Acts typically mandate settlement within 2 to 7 days of termination. Unreasonable withholding of F&F dues entitles the employee to file a complaint before the Labour Commissioner.

Gratuity Dues: Under the Payment of Gratuity Act 1972, employees completing 5 years of continuous service are entitled to gratuity calculated as (15 days' salary × number of years of service / 26).

Non-Compete and Restraint of Trade: Under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act 1872, post-employment non-compete clauses prohibiting an employee from taking up employment with a competitor are void and unenforceable in India.

Redressal Forums:
1. Labour Commissioner / Conciliation Officer: Initial forum for filing complaints regarding unpaid dues or illegal termination.
2. Labour Court / Industrial Tribunal: For adjudication if conciliation fails.
3. Civil Court / High Court: For breach of contract claims (especially for executive/managerial personnel).
